This folio (15r) is a dense scratch sheet of number-theoretic computation, with no connected prose and no stated problem. The previous page (12) holds similar material: lists of residues grouped by braces, numbered 990-1000, with factorizations such as 3.5.11. The next page carries headings such as 'Ord. 1, 2, 3, 6', determinants like -102, -104, -115, -119 and -123, and continued-fraction style forms (b+sqrt D)/a. The context therefore looks like Gauss's work on classes, orders and genera of binary quadratic forms (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, Section V) and on tables of reduced forms for negative determinants. That reading is my inference from context, not something stated on the page.

Left block (about 40% of the page): five columns of headed number groups. The headings run 137-142 in column 1, 43 (probably a mis-transcribed or re-written 143), 144-148 in column 2, and 149 and 150 in column 3. Under each heading is a short list of small integers (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13...) bracketed in groups by curly braces. A dash or a small product follows some braces (for example 147, 8, 8.25, 4.8.4, 8.47, 11.13, 8.29, 73, 7, 149, 4.8). The first entry is always 1. The most natural reading is that for a modulus or determinant numbered 137-150 Gauss lists residues or classes, groups them into cosets or cycles under a multiplier, and records the group order or the cycle lengths (the products such as 4.8 or 8.29). I cannot determine the exact rule from this page alone. Some of the right-hand annotations, such as 8.25, 8.47 and 8.29, may be struck through, so they are unclear.

Middle and right blocks: loose arithmetic jottings. Examples are 43.29 with 1717 (=17.101) and 40841, 52441, 53429; 988 with 2.13.19; 1044 and 984 and 980; 1756, 194, 2916 (=54^2), 108, 9604 (=98^2), 10584 (=2^3.3^3.7^2), 392, 49; 874; 1269, 14, 37, 2349 (=3^4.29), 87; 2.11.437 and 2.11.19.23 (=9614, with 437=19.23); 5639, 321, 351; 15390 (=2.3^4.5.19), 190, 125.63; and the final run 9614, 9630, 1070, 10098, 9774, 9775. These are factorizations and trial computations, probably checking that particular numbers are represented by, or are norms of, forms of a given determinant. Several entries look like quantities of the form x^2+D y^2 or a product of small primes, but I cannot tell the determinant.

Two pair-tables of 'x,y' values appear, such as 1,0 / 3,1 / 9,1 / 27,10 / 4,0 / 12,4 / 29,8 / 5,0 / 8,2 / 24,22 / 15,5 / 24,10 / 23,3. A second one reads 1,0 4,4 27,22 81,76 70,46 ... 25,19 75,19 and so on. They are likely pairs (a, b) or (x, y) tracing orbits or chains of reduced forms, or powers of a form (3, 9, 27 ... in the first slot suggest successive powers or cyclic composition). A vertical bar table with entries 1, 4, 24, 24, 9, 29, 5, 20 beside 8, 3, 12, 23, 27, 15 with circled (5) and (7) looks like a partition of residues into two classes and a cycle structure. The labels (5) and (7) are probably primes. A final block of prime numbers is not present on this page. It occurs on the next page, which lists primes with 7, 5, 3 labels.

No derivation is stated, so nothing here can be restated as a proof. I mark everything above as interpretation, not reading. The page is best described as raw computational data for class-structure tables of binary quadratic forms or for residue-cycle structure of moduli 137-150.
